market_context.summary: Nigeria is now Jumia's largest market by sales (GMV up 30% year on year in the third quarter of 2026), and Jumia remains the largest transactional marketplace by every traffic estimate retrieved; the classifieds site Jiji draws a comparable or larger audience, while Konga's measurable Nigerian traffic is much smaller. Temu entered in late 2024 and immediately topped the app-download charts, and quick-commerce apps (Chowdeck, Glovo) are adding groceries, pharmacy and their own dark stores. Branded mass-market personal care is listed most completely by small online supermarkets and pharmacies (Supermart.ng and 24 Hours Market in Lagos, and MedPlus), which are openly readable; some international brands are thin or absent on Jumia (for example, a Pantene search returned no results). No official statistic on Nigerian e-commerce or online beauty sales was found, and commercial market-size estimates conflict so widely that none is reproduced here. Social selling through Instagram, WhatsApp or TikTok could not be evidenced in this session beyond platform reach figures.

key_facts.fact: Nigeria overtook Cote d'Ivoire as Jumia's largest market by sales in the first quarter of 2026, when Nigerian GMV grew 42% year on year (company statements reported by Semafor).
Jumia reported Nigerian GMV up 30% year on year in the third quarter of 2026, with broad-based growth across categories. Country-level GMV and customer numbers are Not publicly disclosed.
Jumia group (all eight countries, physical goods): GMV US$224.0 million, 2.7 million quarterly active customers and 6.3 million orders in the third quarter of 2026.

Jumia Nigeria's most-sold product groups in 2024 by gross items were phones, beauty and perfumes, home and men's clothing, and 24.7 million products were listed on Jumia Nigeria. Dated: internal data as of December 2024.
key_facts.source_date: n.d. (2025; internal data as of December 2024)

key_facts.fact: Jiji reports more than 12 million monthly users, more than 5 million ads with a listed value above US$15 billion, and over 40 million visits in the first quarter of 2026.
Temu became the most downloaded app in Nigeria on both Android and Apple app stores within weeks of starting to advertise there in late 2024 (Similarweb data cited by Semafor). Dated.

Website traffic, October 2026 (Semrush estimates; share from Nigeria in brackets): jumia.com.ng 5.93M visits (76.14%), jiji.ng 4.34M (63.2%), konga.com 1.40M (46.89%), chowdeck.com 715.4K (42.13%), supermart.ng 105.4K (86.44%). Similarweb's free pages show higher totals for jumia.com.ng (9.2M, 58.04% from Nigeria) and jiji.ng (8.1M, 45.4%) and 1.8M for konga.com, of which only 21.85% is from Nigeria.
Chowdeck had about 1.5 million customers when it raised a US$9 million Series A in August 2025 and was opening dark stores for grocery delivery in 20 minutes or less. Dated: about 15 months old.
Nigeria had 109 million internet users (45.5% penetration) at the end of 2025; TikTok's adult advertising reach was 47.8 million, Facebook's 38.0 million and Instagram's 10.0 million.

Dedicated beauty-retail apps are negligible: the five most-downloaded beauty retail apps on Android in Nigeria each recorded only tens to a few hundred downloads a week in the first quarter of 2026 (Sensor Tower).

ranking_method_note: weighted_score = 0.20 x ecommerce_significance + 0.25 x beauty_category_relevance + 0.20 x consumer_reach + 0.15 x brand_competitor_coverage + 0.20 x data_integration_feasibility, each scored 1-5, rounded to 2 decimals. priority_rank orders platforms by weighted_score within the country (1 = highest); ties are broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach, as the rubric requires. Where platforms were still tied, ecommerce_significance, then data_integration_feasibility, then name were used (our addition; the rubric stops earlier). Scores are analyst judgements anchored to the evidence note beside each score. Anchors for brand_competitor_coverage (thirteen reference brands): 5 = at least 11 confirmed with real depth, or every brand tested when at least 8 were tested; 4 = 8-10 confirmed, or 11+ confirmed with thin listings; 3 = 4-7 confirmed; 2 = 1-3 confirmed; 1 = none found. Where a catalogue could not be read at all the score is a placeholder marked UNVERIFIED: 3 (neutral) for pharmacies, grocers and general marketplaces that normally stock the category, 2 for delivery apps and classifieds, 1 for cross-border value or fashion platforms and private messaging. competitor_presence.level follows the same evidence: high = score 4-5, medium = 3, low = 1-2, unknown = placeholder. Anchors for data_integration_feasibility: 5 = documented seller API plus openly readable pages, 4 = openly readable pages or feeds, 3 = partly readable or seller-portal access only, 2 = automated access refused, 1 = app-only, login wall or CAPTCHA. Closed platforms therefore rank lower for reasons of access, not commercial weight. For Nigeria this mainly affects Jiji and Konga, and it lifts small open sites such as Supermart.ng and 24 Hours Market above much larger platforms.
